title: Forever with the Lord
description: Forever with the Lord in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 231, “Forever with the Lord”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: For-ev-er with the Lord! So, Fa-ther, let it be; Life from the dead is in that word, 'Tis im-mor-tal-i-ty.

lines: Life from the dead is in that word,
Yet nightly pitch my moving tent
Home of my soul, how near
At times to faith's foreseeing eye
I hear at morn and even,
And then I feel, that He,
The Lord, is never far from me,
The promise of that blessed word
Be Thou at my right hand,
Uphold Thou me, and I shall stand;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
